# Platform reference

What the Base Profile gives an applet: its APIs, their types, the platform's errors, and the kinds of trap. This page is generated from the [Base Profile](https://github.com/cardlang/cardlang/blob/main/platform/base-profile.md), its [API catalog](https://github.com/cardlang/cardlang/blob/main/platform/base-catalog.txt) and the [specification](https://github.com/cardlang/cardlang/blob/main/language/spec/00-index.md), so it always matches them. They are the authority; [chapter 8](08-platform.md) explains how to use the APIs.

Every API returns an outcome. Its errors are listed in precedence order: when several apply, it returns the first (*BP-8*). When an API fails, nothing changes, unless its entry says otherwise (*BP-7*).

## Keys: `card.key`

### `card.key.generate`

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
card.key.generate(id: u32, spec: KeySpec)
```

Create key id with fresh random material; for EcP256Private, a key pair (BP-20).

- **Types:** [`KeySpec`](#keyspec)
- **Errors:** [`AlreadyExists`](#carderror-alreadyexists), [`Unsupported`](#carderror-unsupported), [`Malformed`](#carderror-malformed), [`Capacity`](#carderror-capacity)
- **In a transaction:** takes part: undone if the transaction aborts
- **Resources:** creates Key(id)

### `card.key.import`

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
card.key.import(id: u32, spec: KeySpec, material: ref u8[])
```

Create key id from raw AES bytes, a P-256 private scalar or an uncompressed P-256 point (BP-21).

- **Types:** [`KeySpec`](#keyspec)
- **Errors:** [`AlreadyExists`](#carderror-alreadyexists), [`Malformed`](#carderror-malformed), [`Capacity`](#carderror-capacity)
- **In a transaction:** takes part: undone if the transaction aborts
- **Resources:** creates Key(id)

### `card.key.export_public`

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
card.key.export_public(id: u32, output: inout u8[]) -> u32
```

Write the 65-byte uncompressed public point of a P-256 key and return 65 (BP-22).

- **Errors:** [`NotFound`](#carderror-notfound), [`WrongResourceType`](#carderror-wrongresourcetype), [`Capacity`](#carderror-capacity)
- **In a transaction:** takes effect at once, even inside a transaction
- **Resources:** uses Key(id)

### `card.key.delete`

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
card.key.delete(id: u32)
```

Delete key id and erase its material (BP-23).

- **Errors:** [`NotFound`](#carderror-notfound), [`WrongResourceType`](#carderror-wrongresourcetype)
- **In a transaction:** takes part: undone if the transaction aborts
- **Resources:** deletes Key(id)

## Types

The profile's types, declared in [`base-types.card`](https://github.com/cardlang/cardlang/blob/main/platform/base-types.card). Every applet is built with them, so their names are taken.

<a id="keytype"></a> <a id="keystorage"></a> <a id="keyspec"></a>

Keys (§7). Each value names one valid key type; later versions add values for new curves and sizes.

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
enum KeyType {
    Aes128;
    Aes256;
    EcP256Private;
    EcP256Public;
    Hmac256;
}

enum KeyStorage {
    Persistent;
    Volatile;
    Command;
}

struct KeySpec {
    type: KeyType;
    storage: KeyStorage;
}
```

<a id="digestalgorithm"></a> <a id="macalgorithm"></a> <a id="signaturealgorithm"></a> <a id="kdfalgorithm"></a> <a id="cipheralgorithm"></a>

Cryptographic operations (§8). One enum per family, so a wrong algorithm is a compile-time error.

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
enum DigestAlgorithm {
    Sha256;
}

enum MacAlgorithm {
    HmacSha256;
}

enum SignatureAlgorithm {
    EcdsaP256Sha256;
}

enum KdfAlgorithm {
    HkdfSha256;
}

enum CipherAlgorithm {
    AesCbcNoPadding;
}
```

<a id="operationlifetime"></a>

Multi-part operations (§8, B5).

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
enum OperationLifetime {
    Command;
    Session;
}
```

<a id="cbormajor"></a> <a id="cborhead"></a>

CBOR (§9). The major types of RFC 8949, and a decoded head.

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
enum CborMajor {
    Unsigned;
    Negative;
    Bytes;
    Text;
    Array;
    Map;
    Tag;
    Simple;
}

struct CborHead {
    major: CborMajor;
    argument: u32;
    size: u32;
}
```

<a id="tlvclass"></a> <a id="tlvhead"></a>

BER-TLV (§10). The tag is its raw bytes packed into a u32, big-endian, as card specifications write it.

<!-- check: none -->
```cardlang
enum TlvClass {
    Universal;
    Application;
    ContextSpecific;
    Private;
}

struct TlvHead {
    tag: u32;
    class: TlvClass;
    constructed: bool;
    length: u32;
    size: u32;
}
```

## The platform's errors

The members of `CardError`, with their codes (*BP-12*). The host sees category `02` and the code in the raw binding, or status word `6F00` plus the code in the ISO 7816 binding.

| Member | Code | Returned by |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="carderror-overflow"></a>`CardError.Overflow` | `0001` | Checked arithmetic (EXP-29) |
| <a id="carderror-underflow"></a>`CardError.Underflow` | `0002` | Checked arithmetic (EXP-29) |
| <a id="carderror-divisionbyzero"></a>`CardError.DivisionByZero` | `0003` | Checked arithmetic (EXP-29) |
| <a id="carderror-conversionrange"></a>`CardError.ConversionRange` | `0004` | `checked_convert` (EXP-33) |
| <a id="carderror-notfound"></a>`CardError.NotFound` | `0010` | Unknown resource identifier (PLT-22) |
| <a id="carderror-alreadyexists"></a>`CardError.AlreadyExists` | `0011` | Creating a resource whose identifier is in use (PLT-22) |
| <a id="carderror-wrongresourcetype"></a>`CardError.WrongResourceType` | `0012` | A resource of the wrong kind (PLT-22) |
| <a id="carderror-invalidstate"></a>`CardError.InvalidState` | `0013` | A multi-part operation used out of order |
| <a id="carderror-capacity"></a>`CardError.Capacity` | `0014` | Not enough resource capacity, or an output view too short (BP-6) |
| <a id="carderror-unsupported"></a>`CardError.Unsupported` | `0020` | An algorithm, size or value the platform does not provide |
| <a id="carderror-malformed"></a>`CardError.Malformed` | `0021` | Input that is not well-formed, or not canonical where canonical form is required |

## Trap kinds

The kinds of trap (*RTF-4*). Scenarios name them in `expect trap`, and `clc run` and the debugger show them. The host usually learns only that a trap happened, not its kind (*PLT-10*).

| Kind | Raised when | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `OVERFLOW` | An arithmetic result is above its type's maximum, or the signed minimum is divided by −1 | EXP-23, EXP-24 |
| `UNDERFLOW` | An arithmetic result is below its type's minimum, including unsigned subtraction below zero | EXP-23 |
| `DIV-ZERO` | The divisor of `/` or `%` is zero | EXP-24 |
| `NEGATION` | The signed minimum is negated | EXP-25 |
| `SHIFT` | A shift count is at least the width of the left operand | EXP-26 |
| `BOUNDS` | An index, a slice, an element reference, or the argument length of `decode_be`/`decode_le` is out of range, or the two sides of a slice assignment differ in length | EXP-37, EXP-39, STM-9, FUN-11, FUN-20, FUN-24 |
| `RESPONSE-COUNT` | The command returns a count larger than `response.length` | HEP-9 |
| `TXN-CAPACITY` | A capacity of the target is exceeded at runtime: a transaction's capacity, or the atomic-update capacity for a destination whose size is known only at runtime | TXN-16, STA-13 |
| `COMMIT` | A commit fails in a way the platform contains | TXN-12 |
| `NESTED-TXN` | A runtime nesting check fails. Accepted programs never reach this (TXN-10) | TXN-10 |
| `EXHAUSTED` | The command exhausts its execution budget, or a runtime stack check fails. Accepted programs never reach the stack case (RTF-7) | RTF-6, RTF-7 |
| `VM` | The VM finds an invalid instruction or invalid state. Verified programs never reach this | — |
